title: Bolzano's Theorem for Polynomials: Odd Degree Forces a Real Root

problemStatement.plain: Every real polynomial of odd degree has a real root. This is the classical corollary of the Intermediate Value Theorem; the genuine content is showing that an odd-degree polynomial actually attains both a negative and a positive value, which discharges the IVT hypothesis rather than assuming it.
whyMatters: Real-analytic analogue of the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra: pins down exactly which real polynomials are forced to have real roots by continuity (odd degrees only).
Forces the odd half of the classification of ℝ-irreducible polynomials (degree ≤ 2).

knownResults.goal: Prove odd-degree real polynomials have a real root, VERIFIED and axiom-free.

currentState.focus: Completed: verified 0-axiom proof plus gallery integration.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: VERIFIED 0-axiom proof of Bolzano for polynomials (4 theorems) with gallery integration.
insights: Mathlib provides polynomial end-behavior only at +∞ (tendsto_atTop/atBot with the atTop input filter). The -∞ end is obtained by reflection: compose with -X so P.comp(-X)(y) = P(-y); leadingCoeff_comp negates the leading coefficient exactly when the degree is odd (c·(-1)^n).
intermediate_value_univ₂ over all of ℝ avoids ordering the two sign-change points a, b or managing an Icc.
Reducing to positive leading coefficient via -P (same roots, same odd degree) halves the case analysis.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has no 'odd-degree real polynomial has a root' lemma, nor a 'tendsto at atBot input filter' polynomial asymptotic; the reflection workaround fills the latter.
nextSteps: Optional follow-up: assemble the full ℝ-irreducible classification (degree ≤ 2) by combining this odd-degree half with a degree-2 discriminant analysis.
Optional follow-up: Cauchy root bound to turn existence into an explicit bracketing for the bisection entries in this IVT family.
knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: intermediate-value-theorem-oq-04

## Problem
Every real polynomial of odd degree has a real root (Bolzano's corollary of the IVT).

## Result (COMPLETE, VERIFIED, 0-axiom)
Four theorems in `Proofs/IntermediateValueTheoremOQ04.lean`:
- `exists_neg_and_pos_of_pos_leadingCoeff` — sign attainment.
- `exists_root_of_both_signs` — IVT wrapper via `intermediate_value_univ₂`.
- `exists_root_of_odd_natDegree` — the main theorem.
- `not_irreducible_of_odd_natDegree_ge_three` — structural corollary.

## Key technique
The missing -∞ asymptotic is realised by composing with `-X`: `P.comp(-X)(y) = P(-y)` and `leadingCoeff (P.comp(-X)) = leadingCoeff P · (-1)^{deg P} = -c` for odd degree, so the reflected polynomial runs to -∞ at +∞ and supplies a negative value of P.

## Mathlib lemmas used
`tendsto_atTop_of_leadingCoeff_nonneg`, `tendsto_atBot_of_leadingCoeff_nonpos`, `natDegree_comp`, `leadingCoeff_comp`, `Odd.neg_one_pow`, `intermediate_value_univ₂`, `Polynomial.continuous`, `dvd_iff_isRoot`, `Irreducible.isUnit_or_isUnit`, `natDegree_X_sub_C`.
